skill.name: offer-claims-registry
skill.description: Maintains an append-only registry for marketing claims and offers, including exact wording, evidence, disclosures, terms, review dates, and usage. Supports controlled proposals, owner decisions, queries, expiry, and generated views without inventing substantiation or legal conclusions.
skill.summary: Register and trace marketing claims, supporting evidence, disclosures, and offer terms through a controlled event workflow.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: All 30 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, fixed documentation links, metadata URLs, and constrained repository commands. The skill requires explicit permission for registry writes and shows no prompt injection, exfiltration, or malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Marketing teams lose track of approved claims, evidence, disclosures, and offer dates. This skill maintains an append-only registry with controlled proposals and review workflows.
actual_capabilities: Queries current claim and offer records by aggregate identifier.
Prepares proposals with exact wording, evidence provenance, disclosures, scope, and review dates.
Tracks offer terms, eligibility, destinations, start dates, expiry dates, and linked claims.
Supports authorized acceptance, rejection, updates, expiry, and withdrawal through append-only events.
Preserves unresolved evidence gaps instead of converting unsupported assertions into approved claims.
Regenerates human-readable claim and offer views from accepted projection state.
limitations: Standalone installations can prepare proposals but cannot append events, project state, or grant canonical approval.
The skill does not invent evidence, legal conclusions, or performance claims.
Concrete advertisement and disclosure compliance requires a separate auditor.
Registry mutations require explicit permission, the shared runtime, and an authorized host capability.

use_cases.title: Register a substantiated claim
use_cases.description: Record exact wording, evidence scope, disclosure, usage, and the next review date.

use_cases.title: Review pending proposals
use_cases.description: Accept supported proposals, reject weak evidence, and preserve every decision in event history.

use_cases.title: Check a live offer
use_cases.description: Confirm current terms, eligibility, destination, linked claims, and expiry before publishing a campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Look up an offer
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the accepted terms, status, eligibility, and expiry for offer {offer_id}. Include evidence gaps and the latest projection revision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup before using an offer

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a claim proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a proposal for claim {claim_id} with exact wording, evidence source, scope, disclosure, usage, and review date.

prompt_templates.title: Review pending claims
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pending claim proposals in offset order. Recommend acceptance or rejection for each proposal and explain unresolved evidence gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evidence review by an authorized owner

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile the registry
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile accepted claims with current evidence and rendered uses. Propose narrower wording, expiry, or withdrawal where scope or dates no longer match.

output_examples.input: Show the current state of offer summer-2026.
output: Terms: 20 percent off eligible annual plans.
Open issue: destination availability needs confirmation before the next campaign.
Proposed wording: Customers reduced setup time by 30 percent.
Evidence: Product study dated 10 July 2026, limited to enterprise onboarding.
Review state: unresolved until audience scope and required disclosure are confirmed.
Accept clm-021 because its wording matches the documented population and measurement window.
Reject clm-022 because the source does not support the stated percentage.
Keep clm-023 pending because no evidence source is on file.

best_practices: Store exact approved wording and measurable interpretation, not a loose summary.
Match evidence scope to the audience, market, product version, channel, and time window.
Require explicit permission and preserve proposals, decisions, revisions, and expiry events.
anti_patterns: Do not approve a needs-source marker using the unsupported assertion itself.
Do not edit the event stream or generated views manually.
Do not place host capability values in requests, files, or logs.

faq.question: Can this skill approve a claim without evidence?
faq.answer: No. Missing evidence remains unresolved or none-on-file until a suitable source supports the wording and scope.

faq.question: Can it write advertising copy?
faq.answer: No. It records accepted wording and terms. A separate creative skill should produce campaign copy.

faq.question: Who can accept or reject proposals?
faq.answer: Only an authorized host-capability principal can make canonical decisions. Ordinary producers submit proposals.

faq.question: What happens when an offer expires?
faq.answer: The owner records a dated state change or tombstone. Earlier approval events remain unchanged.

faq.question: Can I edit the claims ledger directly?
faq.answer: No. The ledger is a generated view of accepted projection state and cannot grant approval.

faq.question: Does the skill perform legal compliance review?
faq.answer: No. It tracks evidence and disclosures. A relevant auditor must assess each concrete use.
